tests.prompt: Call InitDungeon with a connector marked Locked but LockDC<=0. Verify InitDungeon returns an error identifying the offending connector by index, and mutates no encounter data.
Call InitDungeon with a connector marked Locked, LockDC set, but LockAbility empty. Verify InitDungeon returns an error identifying the offending connector by index.

Call InitDungeon on a 3-region dungeon where connector 1 is Locked but invalid. Verify the rejected call leaves Space nil and Doors empty -- the invariant InitDungeon's atomicity contract already guarantees for its other pre-mutation validation gates.

Build a 3-region dungeon (entrance/corridor/boss) where connector 0 is plain and connector 1 is Locked with a DC/Ability/Tool. Verify connector 1's generated DoorData is Locked=true, Open=false, and carries the exact LockDC/LockAbility/LockTool configured; verify connector 0's generated door stays entirely unlocked (Locked=false, LockDC=0, LockAbility/LockTool empty).
Call InitTwoChamberRoom (the compatibility wrapper over InitDungeon). Verify its generated door is never locked -- the wrapper must not gain locked-door behavior as a side effect of #815.

Build a dungeon with a generated locked boss connector, marshal ToData() to JSON, unmarshal, and LoadFromData. Verify the reloaded door's Locked/LockDC/LockAbility/LockTool are intact and it still blocks LoS into the boss region.

Against a generated locked boss door: AttemptUnlock, then SubmitCheck with a roll that fails the DC. Verify the door remains Locked=true, Open=false, still blocks movement/LoS into the boss region, and is recoverable (a second AttemptUnlock succeeds).

Against a generated locked boss door: AttemptUnlock, then SubmitCheck with a roll that passes the DC. Verify Locked clears, Open becomes true (via the existing dispatchPromptAction -> OpenDoor path, no new verb), the entrance becomes reachable through to the boss region, LoS across the doorway clears, and the player's View reveals into the boss chamber through the doorway.

In an N-region InitDungeon (#814) encounter with more than one non-final combat pocket, clearing an early pocket (all monsters in the CURRENT initiative dead) while hostiles remain alive in later, still-unopened regions must exit to FREE_ROAM, not end the encounter.
tests.notes: TestClearingEarlyPockets_ThenVictoryOnLastHostile_ReloadSafe (dungeon_completion_test.go), entrance-pocket-clear assertions. Already-shipped behavior: combat.go's checkPocketCleared (rpg-toolkit#794/#796) already implements exactly this, previously proven only against a hand-built single-door room (combat_pockets_test.go) or InitDungeon's OWN geometry tests (dungeon_test.go, no combat lifecycle) -- never both together. DISCRIMINATION: temporarily short-circuited checkPocketCleared (combat.go) to `return nil` unconditionally (production mutation, reverted immediately) and reran -- failed at the first pocket-clear assertion (Mode stayed ModeTurnBased instead of ModeFreeRoam, Initiative non-empty, ModeChangedEvent absent). Reverted -- GREEN; `git diff origin/main -- combat.go` empty afterward, confirming no unrelated change was kept.

tests.prompt: The same non-terminal pocket-clear-to-FREE_ROAM behavior must hold for a SECOND early pocket too (corridor, cleared after the entrance pocket), not just the first -- proving the rule composes across more than one non-final region, which is the actual gap #817 called for evidence of (every prior test only had 2 pockets total, i.e. only ONE non-final pocket).
tests.notes: TestClearingEarlyPockets_ThenVictoryOnLastHostile_ReloadSafe, corridor-pocket-clear assertions: after the entrance pocket clears, opening door 0 and moving into LoS of the corridor goblin starts a fresh pocket scoped to just that goblin (boss goblin, still behind the closed door 1, is not sighted); clearing it exits to FREE_ROAM a second time, with the boss goblin asserted still alive and untouched. Covered by the same checkPocketCleared discrimination as the row above (both assertions failed together under that mutation).

tests.prompt: Killing the last hostile ANYWHERE in an N-region InitDungeon encounter (here: the boss, in the final region, after two earlier non-terminal pocket-clears) ends the whole encounter, publishing EncounterEndedEvent with the canonical EncounterEndedReasonAllHostilesDefeated -- not a new 'victory' reason string.
tests.notes: TestClearingEarlyPockets_ThenVictoryOnLastHostile_ReloadSafe, final assertions. Already-shipped: death.go's checkEncounterEnd predicate is `len(e.data.Monsters) == 0` -- data.Monsters is one flat map spanning every region/pocket, so this predicate was ALREADY whole-dungeon-scoped by construction, not pocket-scoped -- #817 did not need new victory logic, only end-to-end proof against the real InitDungeon generator with multiple intervening pockets. DISCRIMINATION: temporarily changed the case guard to `case false && len(e.data.Monsters) == 0:` (production mutation, reverted immediately) and reran -- failed exactly as expected (Mode stayed ModeTurnBased/ModeFreeRoam instead of ModeEnded after the boss died; EncounterEndedEvent never published). Reverted -- GREEN; `git diff origin/main -- death.go` empty afterward.

tests.prompt: A TPK inside an N-region dungeon ends the encounter with the existing, canonical EncounterEndedReasonTPK -- firing regardless of how many hostiles are still alive and completely unengaged elsewhere in the dungeon (never even sighted), proving TPK is not gated on hostile-clearing the way victory is, and does not fire the victory reason instead. #817's 'Approved Slice 3 corrections' comment explicitly required NOT inventing new defeat detection -- this test proves the EXISTING declaration composes correctly with the N-region/combat-pocket machinery rather than re-deriving it.
tests.notes: TestTPKMidDungeon_EndsWithCanonicalReason_HostilesRemainElsewhere (dungeon_completion_test.go): solo flat-snapshot alice (1 HP, no DataJSON, same instant-death fallback tpk_test.go's own multi-player test uses) engages only the entrance goblin; EndTurn-cycled to the goblin's turn, NPCAct kills her -> ModeEnded, EncounterEndedReasonTPK -- with the corridor and boss goblins (never sighted, still behind both closed doors) asserted alive and untouched. Gap this closes: every prior TPK test (tpk_test.go) used a flat, single-monster room; no test previously proved TPK still works correctly (and doesn't accidentally trip the victory branch, or get starved by some pocket-scoping regression) inside the N-region/combat-pocket machinery specifically. DISCRIMINATION: temporarily changed death.go's TPK case guard to `case false && e.allPlayersDead():` (production mutation, reverted immediately) and reran -- failed exactly as expected (Mode stayed ModeTurnBased, no EncounterEndedEvent). Reverted -- GREEN; `git diff origin/main -- death.go` empty afterward.

tests.prompt: After either terminal outcome (victory or TPK) inside an N-region dungeon, a ToData/JSON/LoadFromData round trip must preserve Mode == ModeEnded and an empty Initiative -- the fields the toolkit actually persists on Data -- and a post-reload verb call (EndTurn) must be rejected with ErrEncounterEnded rather than resuming as a live, inescapable fight. Reason itself is explicitly NOT asserted post-reload: it lives only on the published EncounterEndedEvent (events/encounter_ended.go), never written onto Data, so there is nothing for LoadFromData to round-trip -- any reason projection for a resumed/reconnecting client is rpg-api's job (#690), out of scope here. This is the 'to the extent the toolkit owns it' boundary #817 draws.
tests.notes: dcAssertReloadSafe, called from both TestClearingEarlyPockets_ThenVictoryOnLastHostile_ReloadSafe and TestTPKMidDungeon_EndsWithCanonicalReason_HostilesRemainElsewhere. Already-shipped: Mode/Initiative are ordinary Data fields serialized via encoding/json and LoadFromData copies data.Mode straight through (encounter.go's LoadFromData only overrides Mode when it is core.ModeUnspecified, never when it is already core.ModeEnded) -- exhaustively proven already for the flat-room TPK case by tpk_test.go's own persistence tests (TestTPK_RunsEndOfCombatSweep_ExitCombatClearsEconomy, TestTPK_DeadFlagDoesNotLeakAcrossEncounters). No additional discrimination performed on the JSON round trip itself (basic Go struct-field marshaling, not toolkit-specific logic) beyond confirming it holds for this N-region/multi-pocket fixture specifically, which was the untested combination.
